newsitem.title: USA: BP/Chevron Alaska find worries Babbitt.
newsitem.headline: BP/Chevron Alaska find worries Babbitt.

text.p: U.S. Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt raised concern Thursday about an oil and natural gas discovery in Alaska by BP Exploration and Chevron USA close to the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
"Based on preliminary information provided to the Department by BP/Chevron, the companies have the commercial possibility of producing oil from this state lease," Babbitt said in a statement.
A spokesman for BP Exploration, a subsidiary of British Petroleum, declined to comment on the find, saying the company would be announcing it later Thursday.
"The Department of Interior's number one concern continues to be the protection of the rich biological resources of the Arctic Refuge," Babbitt said.
"Let me be perfectly clear. This administration remains strongly opposed to oil and gas drilling within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge," he said.

The discovery is on the Sourdough Prospect, a state lease, and Babbitt said the department would work with the state and the companies to make sure the prospect was developed without harming the environment.

"In addition, it is our responsibility to assure that American taxpayers are adequately compensated for any such a potential drainage of federal oil from the state lease, should such a situation arise, without development or surface disturbance of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge," he said.
Chevron had no immediate comment on the discovery.
